jobs.title: Technical Program Manager - EV Charging Platform OCPP & NET Core
jobs.description:
**WHO WE ARE:**

We are an end-to-end Renewable Energy provider. We offer products to commercial and enterprise clients in EV Charging solutions, Fleet Electrification, Solar Micro-grids, Energy storage, Hydroponic farming and Rain Water/Grey Water collection systems. We have been experiencing tremendous growth in all these areas and operate under several government rebate programs that ensure a steady and reliable flow of revenues. Our company handles the entire flow of providing these products and services beginning with Sales, Provisioning, Design and Engineering, Contracting and Construction, Servicing and Maintenance. If you are passionate about the EV industry and working with awesome teams in a fast-growing company, we want to speak with you! Join us in making a meaningful impact!

**JOB SUMMARY**

You will own the delivery of our cloud Charging Station Management System (CSMS): a .NET Core platform that keeps thousands of DC fast chargers and Level 2 stations online, billing correctly, and compliant with OCPP 1.6J and 2.0.1. The chargers are hardware from multiple manufacturers running firmware we do not control; the platform must talk to all of them reliably, at scale, over long-lived WebSocket connections.  
  
This is a hands-on technical program role, not a project-coordination role. You will read OCPP message logs, sit in on architecture reviews, decide when a firmware vendor's deviation from spec gets a workaround versus a pushback, and translate utility, regulator and customer requirements into engineering milestones the team can commit to. You are the single point of accountability for whether the platform roadmap ships on time and interoperates in the field.

You will work across backend engineering, firmware and hardware partners, QA and certification, field operations, and commercial teams, and act as the primary technical interface to charger manufacturers, charge point operators (CPOs), e-mobility service providers (eMSPs) and enterprise fleet customers.

  

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

**Program strategy and roadmap**

Own the CSMS technical roadmap: define program scope, phase gates, success criteria and release cadence, and keep it aligned with commercial commitments and regulatory deadlines.  

Translate business, customer and regulatory requirements into epics, acceptance criteria and milestones engineering can estimate and commit to.  
Run quarterly planning, weekly program reviews and release go/no-go decisions; publish status, risks and decisions to leadership in a form non-engineers can act on.  
Prioritize across competing demands (new charger onboarding, customer integrations, protocol upgrades, platform reliability) with explicit trade-offs, not a growing backlog.  

**OCPP implementation and interoperability**

Oversee implementation and conformance of OCPP 1.6J and 2.0.1 across all supported profiles: Core, Firmware Management, Local Auth List, Reservation, Smart Charging, Remote Trigger, and 2.0.1 functional blocks including Provisioning, Authorization, Transactions, Tariff & Cost, Diagnostics and Security.  

Own the charger onboarding program: define the certification matrix per manufacturer/firmware version, run interoperability test plans, and sign off before a model is approved for field deployment.  
Maintain the known-deviations register: where a vendor's firmware departs from spec, decide between a platform-side workaround, a vendor fix, or declining support, and document the decision.  
Lead the OCPP 1.6J to 2.0.1 migration plan for the installed base, including dual-protocol operation, security profile upgrades (TLS, client certificates), and firmware rollout sequencing.  
Coordinate participation in OCA plugfests and third-party conformance testing; track OCPP 2.1 and ISO 15118-20 readiness.  

**Architecture and engineering partnership**

Partner with .NET Core architects on an event-driven microservices design that handles tens of thousands of concurrent WebSocket sessions, high-frequency MeterValues ingestion, and exactly-once transaction handling.  

Set and enforce non-functional requirements: connection stability, message latency, offline transaction recovery, horizontal scalability, observability and multi-region failover.  
Review technical designs for protocol correctness, backward compatibility and operational risk before implementation starts.  
Ensure the platform exposes clean, versioned APIs for customer portals, mobile apps, fleet management systems, payment processors and OCPI partners.  

**Risk, dependency and quality management**

Identify and mitigate hardware-to-cloud compatibility risks, firmware update bottlenecks, certificate expiry, and cross-team dependencies before they affect field uptime.  

Own the incident review loop for protocol-related outages: root cause, corrective action, and roadmap change if the failure is structural.  
Define release quality bars: automated OCPP conformance tests, load tests against charger simulators, and staged rollouts with rollback criteria.  
Track and report platform KPIs: charger uptime, session success rate, transaction reconciliation accuracy, mean time to onboard a new charger model, and firmware campaign completion rate.  

**Stakeholder, vendor and customer management**

Act as the primary technical interface for charger manufacturers, firmware vendors, utilities, CPOs, eMSPs and enterprise fleet customers.  

Negotiate technical scope, timelines and acceptance criteria with vendors; hold them to delivery and escalate with evidence when they slip.  
Lead customer-facing technical onboarding for large deployments: integration design, cutover plans, pilot acceptance and hypercare.  
Drive hardware certification and compliance workstreams (UL/ETL listing, Energy Star, NEVI/CFI program requirements, utility make-ready and demand-response integrations) in coordination with hardware and compliance teams.  

**Security and compliance**

Own the OCPP 2.0.1 security program: security

We're Winston TCG, a trading card company in Arcadia. We buy a lot of our cards in Japan, grade them, and sell them on stream. We're also opening our first retail store here in Arcadia.

We're a young, fast-growing company, and we're looking for someone who wants to help build out the buying side of the business with us.

The role

This is a data role first. You'd own the numbers behind our card buying and grading operation — what we pay, what grades, what sells, what we net — and turn that into clean reporting leadership can act on each week. From there you'd keep cash and inventory tight and use what the data shows to guide the buyers on what to pick up and what to leave alone.

It's hands-on. You'll split your time between the spreadsheets and the card room.

Here's what you'd be responsible for:

* **The numbers.** Every stream, buying trip, and grading submission tracked: cost, sale price, fees, net. You'd build and own the weekly report — gross, net, margin, ROI by stream and by source — plus the numbers that drive buying decisions, like cost per graded 10, grading hit rate by source, and which cards and sets are actually moving on which platform. Getting that built is the first thing you'd do.
* **Cash.** Our buyers travel with cash to Japan and to shows. You'd issue it, log it, and reconcile every trip within a couple of days of the team getting back.
* **Inventory and the grading pipeline.** Cards come in, get checked, go out to grading, and come back for stream. You'd know where everything is, what it cost, and what it's worth at every step, and flag cards that aren't likely to grade well before we pay to submit them.
* **Guiding the buyers.** You won't be the one on the floor in Osaka. You'd build the buy lists and the rules the buyers work from — price ceilings, how many copies of a card we need, what's selling and what isn't — and check trip lists against inventory before anyone spends money.
* **The room.** Inventory organized and labeled well enough that when a host asks for a card, someone can find it fast.
* **The team's day to day.** Coordinating schedules and output for the buyers and processors, helping train new people, and giving leadership an honest read on how things are going.
* **Shows and trips.** Supporting card-show runs and Japan trips from the office: buy lists, cash, logistics, and the numbers review afterward.

About you

I don't care much about where you worked before. I care about how you work. The people who do well here have good common sense, keep real numbers, and don't need to be told twice. Here's what I'm looking for:

* You live in spreadsheets. Hand you a messy export and you'll come back with the three numbers that matter, not a 20-tab workbook.
* You're tight with cash. Every dollar is accounted for, every trip is reconciled, and you don't need reminding.
* You handle curve balls. Shipment's late, show was a bust, someone bought off the list — you deal with it that day and then put a rule in place so it doesn't happen again.
* You have good sense. I'll give you the goal and the context. I won't always have a procedure written down, and I need you to make the right call anyway.
* You tell me straight. If something's not working, I want to hear it from you with the numbers, not find out later.
* You like cards or you're curious about them. You don't need to be a Pokémon expert — the team has that — but you'll need to learn how to check condition in your first couple of months.

Requirements

**Must have**

* Bachelor's degree, ideally in business, accounting, finance, economics, supply chain, or something similar
* 3+ years running day-to-day operations where you were directly accountable for inventory or cash: retail, warehouse, e-commerce, or a business you ran yourself
* Advanced Excel / Google Sheets: pivot tables, lookups, and tracking sheets you built from scratch. We'll ask you to take a short Excel test before the first interview.
* Hands-on experience handling and reconciling cash
* Experience coordinating a small team's daily work
* Valid passport and willingness to travel to Japan; valid driver's license for card shows
* Able to pass a background check (this role handles cash and inventory)
* Able to work on-site in Arcadia, CA five days a week
* Authorized to work in the United States

**Nice to have**

* Trading-card experience: buying, selling, or grading (Pokémon, TCG, sports cards)
* Whatnot, eBay, or TikTok Shop selling experience at volume
* Startup or early-stage company experience
* Japanese language ability
* Experience building SOPs and training documents

Compensation and schedule

* **Pay:** $65,000 to $85,000 a year depending on your experience
* **Bonus:** A quarterly bonus based on how the acquisitions team does on net margin. We'll spend the first 90 days together setting fair targets before it kicks in.
* **Schedule:** Full-time, in person at our Arcadia office, Monday through Friday. Some weekends for card shows, and probably one or two trips to Japan a year.
* **Where this goes:** The buying side of the business is growing, and this role grows with it.
* **Benefits:** Paid time off and employee pricing on product

Winston TCG is an equal opportunity employer.

Pay: $65,000.00 - $85,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Employee discount

Application Question(s):

* How many years have you managed day-to-day operations with direct accountability for inventory or cash
* Rate your Excel/Google Sheets skill: Basic / Intermediate / Advanced
* Have you personally handled and reconciled cash in a previous job?
* Have you coordinated or led the daily work of a team of 3 or more?

Education:

* Bachelor's (Required)

Work Location: In person

jobs.description:
Description:

This position will report to and operate within CV3 Financial Services, a dedicated subsidiary of CV3 Holdings.

CV3 Financial Services provides financing for non-owner-occupied investment properties, providing flexible loan solutions combined with the experience our customers can trust.

CV3 is more than just a lender. We partner with our customers to accelerate real estate opportunities and are invested in their success. We leverage the best technology to eliminate complexity and simplify the loan process, while never losing sight of the value of building personal relationships with our customers.

We’ve set the bar high. The aspirational mission is to be the #1 choice as a trusted capital partner for real estate investors. We are ready when you are!

**Our People are Our Power**

Great people make great companies. CV3 has nurtured a people-first culture, an entrepreneurial team, and a disciplined craft that fuels innovation and delivers results. We create lasting client relationships based on trust and transparency. We cultivate these relationships by taking amazing care of our people and our customers. Above all, what sets us apart are our five Core Values, which guide everything we do.

The Business Technology Analyst supports CV3’s lending technology, users, and product-development process. This position serves as the primary point of contact for the Creative Development Helpdesk, administers user access and external broker accounts, supports the development of Borrower Center and Mortgage Cadence Platform, and tests system enhancements and bug fixes before release. This role works closely with business users, department leadership, IT, and software developers to resolve problems, document enhancement requests, test solutions, and improve the systems used throughout the loan lifecycle.

**In this position, you will:**

* Manage the Creative Development Helpdesk in GoTo Resolve; acknowledge tickets within one business hour and respond the same day to tickets received before 4:00 p.m.
* Troubleshoot Borrower Center and Mortgage Cadence Platform processes, functionality, access, account, and permission issues.
* Escalate unresolved issues, communicate status and next steps, and document resolutions.
* Identify recurring support issues and recommend training, documentation, process, or system improvements.
* Administer user accounts, roles, permissions, and access changes; coordinate account creation with IT and maintain accurate records.
* Create and maintain external broker accounts and sites based on approved Broker Request Forms.
* Run the broker-creation RPA daily
* Complete broker requests within established service levels and communicate results or missing information.
* Reproduce and document defects; coordinate with users and developers; and track enhancement and defect items.
* Test enhancements, configurations, and fixes in Staging and QA; document results, retest defects, and perform regression testing.
* Support release validation and post-deployment monitoring and communicate release readiness to department leadership.
* Complete approved Mortgage Cadence Platform configurations and maintain related documentation.
* Create and maintain Outbox emails; test content, formatting, recipient logic, triggers, and data fields before deployment.
* This position may involve handling confidential and sensitive information as part of its daily responsibilities. Employees are expected to exercise discretion and protect all sensitive data, including but not limited to personal information, loan details, business and financial records, and proprietary materials.

**SPECIALTY DISCIPLINE RESPONSIBILITIES:**

Creative Development:

* Translate business needs and user feedback into actionable Azure DevOps tickets with requirements, acceptance criteria, and supporting documentation.
* Work with Compliance & Legal to ensure all CV3 documents are accurate, complete, up to date
* Work with Operations SMEs to ensure document needs are met (disclosures, internal docs, closing docs)
* Facilitate discussions with vendors related to document needs (LOS, GoDocs, etc.)

Requirements:

**Successful candidates will possess:**

* Bachelor’s degree required, or a combination of education and experience.
* 5+ years’ experience working in related field
* Experience with Azure DevOps or a comparable development-tracking platform preferred.
* Mortgage or lending-process knowledge preferred; ability to develop this knowledge required.
* Experience with automation tools, user-access administration, or software testing preferred.
* Knowledge of Borrower Center and Mortgage Cadence Platform administration, configuration, accounts, roles, permissions, and access.
* Experience in software support, business systems, quality assurance, lending operations, or product development preferred.

**NECESSARY KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES AND COMPETENCIES:**

* Excellent written and verbal communication and collaboration skills.
* Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
* Ability to investigate issues independently and escalate when appropriate.
* Ability to learn technical systems, workflows, and administrative tools.
* Ability to prioritize competing requests and meet time-sensitive service expectations.
* Knowledge of helpdesk operations, service-level expectations, ticket prioritization, escalation, and customer support.
* Ability to translate business needs into clear requirements, acceptance criteria, enhancement requests, and defect reports.
* Knowledge of quality assurance practices, including test planning, defect management, regression testing, and release validation.
* Strong troubleshooting, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to monitor automated processes, investigate exceptions, and verify successful completion.
* Strong organization and time-management skills, with the ability to prioritize work, meet deadlines, and maintain accurate records.
* Ability to work

jobs.title: Program Manager, Accounting Operations & Strategy
jobs.description:
**About Anthropic**
-------------------

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

**About the role**
------------------

Anthropic is seeking a Program Manager to join our Accounting organization and help it run as one global team. Accounting is scaling at an unprecedented pace across multiple hubs, and the goals, rhythms, programs, and people that make up the team need to stay connected as we grow. In this role, you will own that connective tissue: the annual goal-setting cycle, the leadership team’s operating cadence, org-wide events and internal communications, and the programs that make a distributed team feel like one.

You will partner with Accounting leadership, the People team, Finance Systems, and hub leads. This is a hands-on role with a lot of range: part chief of staff, part program manager, part culture builder.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

### **Goals and operating rhythm**

* Run the annual goal setting process and the reporting that tracks progress against those goals.
* Look at how the org actually operates (meetings, handoffs, planning cycles, decision making) and fix what isn't working.
* Maintain one org-wide planning calendar that shows close, audit, and team milestones alongside company-wide and team events, so leaders can see the pressure points and plan around them.
* Build and maintain a simple set of org health metrics (attrition, engagement scores, hiring pipeline, training completion, survey trends) and report on them regularly.

### **Leadership and org-wide events**

* Run our extended leadership team (XLT) program, including agendas, meetings, follow-ups, and action items.
* Own planning and agenda for the annual offsite and run the quarterly team all-hands.
* Write the internal updates: a regular team newsletter, plus talking points when leadership needs to explain a change to the whole org.

### **People and culture**

* Coordinate projects across the org that support employee experience programs.
* Partner with the People team to roll out training and development programs for Accounting.
* Review team survey results, identify the themes, and build action plans to address the feedback. Follow through and report back to the team.

**Role Description**

The **Complex Program Manager (CPM)** is a key leadership role within HPE’s Private Cloud and Flex Solutions business, responsible for delivering large-scale, multi-site private cloud solutions as a single integrated program. In this role, you will coordinate multiple HPE technologies, including compute, storage, networking, and software, alongside Deployment Services, Professional Services, Managed Services, Local PMOs, third-party partners, and customer teams to achieve successful business outcomes.

The CPM engages early in the sales lifecycle as part of the Center of Excellence pursuit team, helping ensure solutions are deliverable as sold. Success in this position requires a combination of program management expertise, technical acumen, relationship management, cross-functional leadership, and meticulous attention to detail.

The CPM leads programs that integrate multiple HPE products into a single customer solution, while direct ownership of those products remains with separate business units. **Operating Model**

jobs.description:
**About Vantage**
=================

Vantage powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands.

**Reliability Engineering**

The Reliability Engineering Department is responsible for ensuring the operational health of critical systems and the implementation of Site Operations best practices. This includes evaluating the performance and reliability of critical infrastructure, maintaining operational availability through maintenance programs, and providing technical support to Site Operations teams. The department also collaborates closely with the Design Engineering team to provide feedback for future data center designs.

**Position Overview**

**This role will be based near any of our North America office locations, following our flexible work policy (3 days in-office and 2 days flexible).**

The Sr. Technical Project Manager, Site Deployment - Electrical Design Assurance is responsible for providing operationally focused electrical review and technical assurance for new data center builds, expansions, and major fit-out projects across the North America portfolio. This role represents Site Operations and Site Deployment during design development, page-turn reviews, submittal reviews, RFI responses, commissioning strategy alignment, and movement of design packages toward Issued for Construction drawings.

The position ensures that electrical systems are designed and delivered in a manner that is operable, maintainable, safe, reliable, and aligned with long-term Mission Critical Operations requirements. Working closely with Design Engineering, Construction, Commissioning, Business Operations, and local Site Operations teams, this role brings operator perspective into electrical design decisions before construction execution, procurement, and turnover activities create downstream operational risk.

**Essential Job Functions**

* Serve as the primary Site Deployment representative for electrical design assurance across assigned campuses, projects, and expansions.
* Participate in design page-turn reviews and provide operator-focused comments from concept design through IFC drawing issuance.
* Review electrical design packages, one-line diagrams, specifications, sequences of operation, equipment schedules, load studies, and drawing sets for operability, maintainability, safety, and reliability.
* Review electrical submittals, equipment selections, vendor documentation, and proposed alternates to evaluate operational impact, maintainability requirements, protection strategy, and lifecycle risk.
* Support responses to RFIs related to electrical distribution, equipment access, switching, redundancy, load management, protection coordination, EPMS interfaces, maintenance clearances, and long-term serviceability.
* Evaluate value engineering proposals and design changes to ensure critical operational requirements are not removed, reduced, or compromised without appropriate risk visibility.
* Provide technical input for electrical commissioning strategies, operational acceptance criteria, test scripts, integrated systems testing, energization plans, and turnover readiness expectations.
* Collaborate with Site Deployment TPMs and future MCO teams to ensure electrical design intent is carried forward into construction, commissioning, training, CMMS population, and steady-state operations.
* Capture lessons learned from active operating sites and deployment projects and feed them back into future electrical design standards, templates, and review criteria.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

* Review electrical design milestones including 30%, 60%, 90%, IFC, bulletin, and construction revision packages.
* Assess utility service arrangements, medium-voltage distribution, low-voltage distribution, switchgear, transformers, UPS systems, generators, fuel systems interfaces, transfer schemes, busways, panels, grounding, lightning protection, batteries, and EPMS architecture.
* Validate maintenance access, equipment clearances, working space, switching paths, isolation strategy, arc flash considerations, labeling, redundancy philosophy, and operational workflows within electrical spaces.
* Track design review comments, assigned actions, and open electrical issues through closure with Design Engineering, Construction, Commissioning, and Site Operations stakeholders.
* Participate in recurring design coordination meetings, page turns, constructability reviews, operability reviews, energization planning, and commissioning planning sessions.
* Review MEP coordination impacts where electrical systems interface with mechanical, controls, fire protection, security, architectural, structural, civil, and utility scopes.
* Provide operator perspective on sequence of operations, switching procedures, alarm strategy, metering, trending capability, EPMS points, electrical safety requirements, and emergency operating scenarios.
* Review proposed equipment substitutions or manufacturer deviations for potential impacts to maintainability, spare parts, training, warranty, resilience, and operational standardization.
* Support development of operational design standards, electrical review checklists, lessons learned repositories, and acceptance criteria used by the Site Deployment organization.
* Partner with local MCO leadership to ensure future operators understand electrical design intent, operating limitations, maintenance requirements, and known risk items prior to turnover.

**Job Requirements**

* 5+ years of experience in data center operations, electrical engineering, commissioning, critical facilities maintenance, construction QA/QC, or mission-critical infrastructure

new_jobs.description:
**About Gather AI**  
Are you ready to build the future of supply chain? At Gather AI, we're not just creating software; we're pioneering a new era of warehouse intelligence. We've developed a groundbreaking, vision-powered platform that uses autonomous drones and existing equipment to capture real-time data, completely digitizing workflows that have historically been manual and error-prone. This means facilities operate smarter, safer, and more efficiently, ultimately redefining "on-time, in full" delivery.  
If you're looking for an opportunity to contribute to truly transformative technology and make a significant impact in a vital industry, Gather AI is the place for you. We're leading the charge in the rapidly evolving robotics industry, and we invite you to join us in reshaping the global supply chain, one intelligent warehouse at a time.  
**About the Team**  
Gather AI's Hardware team designs, builds and supports the hardware behind our platform: autonomous inventory drones and camera systems that mount on customers' material handling equipment (MHE). The team includes hardware engineers and technicians who work out of the Pittsburgh HQ. Hardware designs and builds new product implementations, reviews and repairs RMAs, and performs detailed analysis of field failures while Field Ops runs day-to-day customer site support.  
**About the role**  
Our robots are already working in customer warehouses, and every new deployment depends on the right hardware arriving built, configured and ready. In this role, you'll own the hardware side of that: deployment readiness, field hardware escalations and returns, and accurate documentation of deployment configurations and bill of materials (BOMs) across Hardware programs. This is an ownership role and much of the processes behind it are yours to build collaboratively with Hardware leadership. As our Hardware Deployment & Development Coordinator, you'll be the hardware team's hub between development and field operations: making sure each deployment's hardware is ready on time, owning how we handle field hardware issues and returns, and keeping our bills of materials and fleet configurations accurate across all our hardware programs. You'll report to our Director of Hardware and work closely with engineers, technicians, Field Ops, Purchasing and customer implementation teams.  
**What you'll do**

* Own hardware readiness for each customer deployment: build schedules, kit lists, parts status, shipping and site prerequisites.
* Be on site for installs and go-lives as the hardware liaison lead, then hand off cleanly to Field Ops.
* Own tier-2 hardware escalations: triage, route to the right technician or engineer, and close the loop.
* Own our RMA process: intake, disposition, failure analysis coordination and trend reporting back to engineering and suppliers.
* Own BOM accuracy and configuration management across programs, including revision control and serial/config traceability.
* Build and document the processes behind the work, including the readiness checklist, RMA workflow and configuration control.
* Plan development builds and test assets with engineering and the technicians, and turn field findings into engineering action.
* Coordinate development builds, test assets and technician schedules, and turn field findings into engineering action.
* Give Purchasing a clear demand plan and flag long-lead and single-source risks early.

**What you bring**

* You've owned hardware readiness for deployments, production launches or NPI builds end to end —, covering schedules, kits, parts and handoffs — and kept other teams moving toward the date without direct authority.
* You've owned the record of what hardware is built and implemented: BOMs and revisions, configurations and change control, or RMA processes. Ideally you've build one of these, not just owned it.a BOM or configuration record, an inventory system or an RMA process.
* You can read assembly and part drawings, electrical schematics, and understand critical to quality callouts. drawings and harness pinouts, and you're comfortable getting hands-on to troubleshoot hardware.
* You can take a field escalation from first report to resolution and keep everyone informed along the way.
* You're detail-oriented, agile and adaptable and adapt quickly when plans change.

**Nice to have**

* Experience in warehouse, material handling or forklift environments.
* Robotics or autonomous-vehicle deployment experience.
* Experience working with suppliers or contract manufacturers on ECOs or recurring defects.Experience coordinating with suppliers or contract manufacturers.
* Experience with Document Control, Good Documentation Practices, and Good Manufacturing Practices.

**Location** Pittsburgh, PA (on site) or remote in the US. About one week a month on site in Pittsburgh; when a customer deployment is active, travel to that site takes priority. Eastern time zone is a plus.  
**How we hire** A recruiter conversation, a conversation with the hiring manager, a practical deployment-planning exercise, and a final round with the team. We'll tell you before each step whether AI tools are welcome.

new_jobs.description:
**Company Description**

**Redica Systems** is the Intelligence Cloud for life sciences, transforming regulatory complexity into connected, proactive intelligence. Redica's platform helps the world's leading Pharmaceutical and MedTech companies stay inspection-ready, manage supplier risk, and keep pace with evolving global regulations. Built on the Redica Catalyst Platform and powered by Redica ID, Redica unifies the industry's most complete regulatory and inspection datasets, sourced from hundreds of global health authorities, into trusted intelligence for quality and regulatory teams. The Redica Intelligence Cloud brings data together to anticipate risk, accelerate compliance, and enable smarter, faster decisions across the enterprise.

More information is available at redica.com.

 **Job Description**

Redica Systems is looking for an Associate Data Analyst to develop customer-facing reports and dashboards using our regulatory intelligence data.

You'll translate customer requests into clear reporting requirements, work with data covering inspections, observations, warning letters, and enforcement actions, and present findings through dashboards, executive reports, and compelling data storytelling.

We're looking for someone who's analytical, detail-oriented, and comfortable using AI to improve how they work. Just as important is a practical, down-to-earth approach and the ability to communicate clearly with customers and colleagues.

**Core Responsibilities**

* Translate customer reporting requests into precise, scoped queries using Redica tools, including Sigma, Claude, and Redica MCP, to identify and extract the right underlying data.
* Build, customize, and publish customer-facing reports, including workbooks, data elements, and visualizations tailored to each customer’s needs.
* Own the full report lifecycle, from intake and data identification through build, QA, proofing, and delivery.
* Interpret and validate data outputs for accuracy before any customer-facing delivery. This is not a “pull and send” role; judgment about data quality and relevance is required.
* Navigate regulatory intelligence data, including FDA enforcement actions, Form 483 observations, warning letters, and inspection records, to answer customer-specific questions through structured reporting.
* Manage multiple concurrent customer deliverables with accuracy and on-time delivery.

**About You**

* **Business Insight:** You understand customer reporting needs and how accurate regulatory intelligence data helps customers answer business-critical questions. You can connect data outputs to the customer’s underlying need, not just the literal request.
* **Manages Complexity:** You break down ambiguous reporting requests into clear steps, including data identification, query logic, report building, QA, and delivery. You can work through complex regulatory datasets without losing accuracy or structure.
* **Decision Quality:** You use data, context, and sound judgment to validate outputs, identify anomalies, and confirm that the final result answers the question being asked. You know when to escalate unclear, incomplete, or questionable results.
* **Collaboration & Influence:** You work effectively with internal teams to clarify requests, resolve data questions, and deliver accurate customer-ready work. You communicate clearly and help keep deliverables moving without unnecessary back-and-forth.
* **Tech Savvy:** You are comfortable working with BI tools, structured data, SQL, AI-assisted tools, and analytics workflows. You learn new systems quickly and use technology to improve accuracy, speed, and quality of work.
* **Engaged:** You share our values and possess the essential competencies needed to thrive at Redica, as outlined here: https://redica.com/company

  
**Qualifications**  

* Bachelor’s degree in data analytics, business analytics, information systems, life sciences, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* 1–3 years of experience in data analysis, business intelligence, reporting, data operations, or a related role.
* Hands-on experience building reports, workbooks, data elements, or visualizations in a cloud BI or analytics tool, such as Sigma, Tableau, Looker, or Power BI; Sigma experience is strongly preferred.
* Working knowledge of SQL, including the ability to write, review, and troubleshoot queries against structured data.
* Experience using AI-assisted tools or natural language data interfaces to support data exploration, query development, or analysis.
* Experience producing accurate, polished work product for internal stakeholders or external customers.

  
**Additional Information**

Top Pharmaceutical Companies, Food Manufacturers, MedTech Companies, and Service Firms from around the globe rely on Redica Systems to mine and process government inspection, enforcement, and registration data. This enables them to quantify risk signals from their suppliers, identify market opportunities, benchmark against peers, and prepare for the latest inspection trends.

Our data and analytics have been cited by major media outlets, including MSNBC, *The Wall Street Journal*, and *The Boston Globe*.

This role is critical to the success of our security operations and will play a key part in evaluating, testing, and deploying emerging technologies and new procedures, ensuring JRM remains proactive in an ever-evolving cybersecurity landscape. The ideal candidate is not only technically proficient but also highly organized, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, maintain detailed documentation, and uphold structured workflows. The Analyst also shares responsibility for incident response.

Reporting directly to the Manager of Information Security, this position offers an exciting opportunity for a security-minded technologist to thrive within a forward-thinking program that values agility, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.

**Key Responsibilities**

Governance & Risk Management:

* Assist in developing, documenting, and enforcing cybersecurity policies, standards, and control procedures.
* Support alignment with frameworks such as NIST CSF, ISO 27001, and CIS Controls.
* Maintain the security risk register and perform technical risk assessments and drive remediation to closure.

Windows IT Administration & Hardening:

* Leverage expertise in Windows Server, Active Directory, DNS, Group Policy, and PowerShell to engineer, automate, and maintain secure system baselines.
* Work with the IT and infrastructure teams to ensure secure configurations and compliance enforcement across the environment.
* Deploy, configure, and tune endpoint management and compliance controls using modern UEM, MDM, and EDR tools.

Identity Security & Access Management:

* Implement identity governance practices, privileged access controls, phishing resistant MFA, and conditional access policy design across Microsoft Entra ID and other third-party IdPs.
* Automate and improve lifecycle management processes, including secure onboarding and offboarding.

Phishing Defense & Awareness:

* Operate a phishing simulation and security awareness platform, run phishing simulations, and report on campaign effectiveness.

Security Engineering & Tooling:

* Design, deploy, and maintain core security platforms, including EDR, SIEM, email security, and vulnerability management.
* Maintain configuration baselines and documentation for deployed security tools.
* Integrate security tools with Microsoft 365, Entra ID, and the broader IT environment to improve visibility and reduce manual effort.
* Run vulnerability scanning, prioritize findings by risk, and coordinate remediation with IT and infrastructure teams.

Detection, Incident Response & Automation:

* Monitor SIEM alerts and dashboards, and tune detections to reduce noise.
* Act as a technical responder in security incidents: triage, investigate, contain, and document root cause and lessons learned.
* Support incident response playbooks and tabletop exercises.
* Automate repetitive security tasks and response workflows using PowerShell, Python, and SOAR or automation platforms.

Innovation & Emerging Technology Evaluation:

* Participate in research, testing, and proof-of-concept (PoC) efforts for new cybersecurity tools, technologies, and frameworks.
* Deploy new technologies and procedures that improve detection, prevention, and governance.

* Familiarity with Microsoft 365, Entra ID (Azure AD), third-party IDP providers, Intune, and modern endpoint security tools.
* Scripting and automation skills in PowerShell.
* Understanding of cybersecurity frameworks and governance models (NIST CSF, ISO 27001, CIS).
* Analytical, collaborative, and adaptable mindset with strong documentation skills.

Preferred:

* Hands-on experience deploying, configuring, and tuning security tools such as EDR, email security, and vulnerability management platforms, or evaluating emerging and cloud security solutions.
* Exposure to SIEM detection engineering and SOAR or automation platforms.
* Experience in risk assessments, audit preparation, or compliance reporting.
* Familiarity with Python, SQL, or Bash/Shell for automation and security analysis.

Each day, our employees solve the most daunting challenges that our customers face. Visit peraton.com to learn how we’re keeping people around the world safe and secure.

##### **Program Overview**

The program is an IDIQ contract for an AWS-based cloud hosting system. Currently, Peraton is supporting the Cloud Security, IoT, and AIML use cases for the environment in a hybrid work environment with Federal employees. Peraton also support the following applications as part of the environment: Dremio, Tableau, Globus, Posit/RStudio, Atlassian, ThingLogix, Alteryx and CloudCheckr.

##### **About The Role**

  

Peraton is seeking a **Junior Business Analyst** **(Data & Integration)** with a strong data analysis background to support NOAA Fisheries data mapping, interoperability requirements, and compliance documentation on a federal data integration program. This role focuses on the technical business analysis activities that bridge data engineering and regulatory compliance.

  

The Department of the Interior (DOI), U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS), and NOAA's National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) have identified a critical gap in the federal government's ability to conduct comprehensive Endangered Species Act (ESA) research. While FWS operates an authoritative web-based platform for managing data for terrestrial and freshwater species, it does not currently include NMFS marine and anadromous species data forcing agencies to rely on separate, manual processes. This program closes that gap by integrating marine and anadromous species data into the existing FWS platform, creating a single, unified experience for all ESA-listed species.

  

**Work Location:** Remote

  

**Day to Day Responsibilities:**

* Conduct detailed source-to-target data mapping analysis for NOAA Fisheries species datasets, documenting field-level transformation rules, data type conversions, and null-handling logic.
* Analyze NOAA Fisheries data quality issues identified during prototype ingestion and document remediation requirements.
* Support the Metadata and Authoritative Source Registry by researching and documenting NOAA Fisheries data source attributes, refresh cadences, and data stewardship contacts.
* Assist in the development and documentation of interoperability testing requirements including API connectivity, data exchange protocols, and metadata alignment test cases.
* Support compliance validation checklist development by documenting validation criteria for species list generation, decision logic, and template content completeness.
* Analyze live consultation feedback from production and document actionable requirements for system updates.
* Support the Prototype Ingest Results Report by documenting NOAA Fisheries data quality issues identified during prototype ingestion, including defect descriptions, root cause analysis, and remediation requirements.
* Assist in the development of training metrics dashboard requirements and reporting specifications.
* Support the compilation of final operational documentation by documenting NOAA Fisheries data refresh procedures.

##### **Qualifications**

  

**Basic Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree with 0 years of professional experience, or a Master’s degree with 0 years of professional experience, or an Associate’s degree with 2 years of professional experience, or a high school diploma/equivalent with 4 years of professional experience.
* U.S. Citizenship required; must have the ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust clearance; all work must be performed within the United States.
* Experience supporting business analysis experience with a focus on data integration or data migration programs.
* Experience with source-to-target data mapping and data quality analysis.
* Familiarity with API integration concepts and interoperability testing requirements.
* Strong analytical and technical documentation skills.
* Experience supporting federal IT programs.
  

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Experience with NOAA Fisheries or other federal environmental data systems.
* Familiarity with ETL concepts, data pipelines, or cloud data platforms.
* Experience supporting compliance validation activities on federal programs.
* Experience contributing to program status reports or monthly progress reports.
* ECBA or CCBA certification.

##### **Details**

**Target Salary Range:** $51,000 - $82,000. This represents the typical salary range for this position. Salary is determined by various factors, including but not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the position, the individual’s experience, education, knowledge, skills, and competencies, as well as geographic location and business and contract considerations. Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay.

**Benefits Statement:** Peraton offers eligible employees a variety of benefits including medical, dental, vision, life, health savings account, short/long term disability, EAP, parental leave, 401(k), paid time off (PTO) for vacation, and company paid holidays. A full listing of available benefits can be viewed at https://www.careers.peraton.com/benefits.

**This role will be based near any of our North America office locations, following our flexible work policy (3 days in-office and 2 days flexible).**

The Sr. Technical Project Manager, Site Deployment - Electrical Design Assurance is responsible for providing operationally focused electrical review and technical assurance for new data center builds, expansions, and major fit-out projects across the North America portfolio. This role represents Site Operations and Site Deployment during design development, page-turn reviews, submittal reviews, RFI responses, commissioning strategy alignment, and movement of design packages toward Issued for Construction drawings.

The position ensures that electrical systems are designed and delivered in a manner that is operable, maintainable, safe, reliable, and aligned with long-term Mission Critical Operations requirements. Working closely with Design Engineering, Construction, Commissioning, Business Operations, and local Site Operations teams, this role brings operator perspective into electrical design decisions before construction execution, procurement, and turnover activities create downstream operational risk.

* Provide technical input for electrical commissioning strategies, operational acceptance criteria, test scripts, integrated systems testing, energization plans, and turnover readiness expectations.
* Collaborate with Site Deployment TPMs and future MCO teams to ensure electrical design intent is carried forward into construction, commissioning, training, CMMS population, and steady-state operations.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

* Provide operator perspective on sequence of operations, switching procedures, alarm strategy, metering, trending capability, EPMS points, electrical safety requirements, and emergency operating scenarios.

* Support development of operational design standards, electrical review checklists, lessons learned repositories, and acceptance criteria used by the Site Deployment organization.
* Partner with local MCO leadership to ensure future operators understand electrical design intent, operating limitations, maintenance requirements, and known risk items prior to turnover.

**Job Requirements**

* 5+ years of experience in data center operations, electrical engineering, commissioning, critical facilities maintenance, construction QA/QC, or mission-critical infrastructure

new_jobs.title: Technical Program Manager - EV Charging Platform OCPP & NET Core
new_jobs.description:
**WHO WE ARE:**

We are an end-to-end Renewable Energy provider. We offer products to commercial and enterprise clients in EV Charging solutions, Fleet Electrification, Solar Micro-grids, Energy storage, Hydroponic farming and Rain Water/Grey Water collection systems. We have been experiencing tremendous growth in all these areas and operate under several government rebate programs that ensure a steady and reliable flow of revenues. Our company handles the entire flow of providing these products and services beginning with Sales, Provisioning, Design and Engineering, Contracting and Construction, Servicing and Maintenance. If you are passionate about the EV industry and working with awesome teams in a fast-growing company, we want to speak with you! Join us in making a meaningful impact!

**JOB SUMMARY**

You will own the delivery of our cloud Charging Station Management System (CSMS): a .NET Core platform that keeps thousands of DC fast chargers and Level 2 stations online, billing correctly, and compliant with OCPP 1.6J and 2.0.1. The chargers are hardware from multiple manufacturers running firmware we do not control; the platform must talk to all of them reliably, at scale, over long-lived WebSocket connections.  
  
This is a hands-on technical program role, not a project-coordination role. You will read OCPP message logs, sit in on architecture reviews, decide when a firmware vendor's deviation from spec gets a workaround versus a pushback, and translate utility, regulator and customer requirements into engineering milestones the team can commit to. You are the single point of accountability for whether the platform roadmap ships on time and interoperates in the field.

You will work across backend engineering, firmware and hardware partners, QA and certification, field operations, and commercial teams, and act as the primary technical interface to charger manufacturers, charge point operators (CPOs), e-mobility service providers (eMSPs) and enterprise fleet customers.

  

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

**Program strategy and roadmap**

Own the CSMS technical roadmap: define program scope, phase gates, success criteria and release cadence, and keep it aligned with commercial commitments and regulatory deadlines.  

Translate business, customer and regulatory requirements into epics, acceptance criteria and milestones engineering can estimate and commit to.  
Run quarterly planning, weekly program reviews and release go/no-go decisions; publish status, risks and decisions to leadership in a form non-engineers can act on.  
Prioritize across competing demands (new charger onboarding, customer integrations, protocol upgrades, platform reliability) with explicit trade-offs, not a growing backlog.  

**OCPP implementation and interoperability**

Oversee implementation and conformance of OCPP 1.6J and 2.0.1 across all supported profiles: Core, Firmware Management, Local Auth List, Reservation, Smart Charging, Remote Trigger, and 2.0.1 functional blocks including Provisioning, Authorization, Transactions, Tariff & Cost, Diagnostics and Security.  

Own the charger onboarding program: define the certification matrix per manufacturer/firmware version, run interoperability test plans, and sign off before a model is approved for field deployment.  
Maintain the known-deviations register: where a vendor's firmware departs from spec, decide between a platform-side workaround, a vendor fix, or declining support, and document the decision.  
Lead the OCPP 1.6J to 2.0.1 migration plan for the installed base, including dual-protocol operation, security profile upgrades (TLS, client certificates), and firmware rollout sequencing.  
Coordinate participation in OCA plugfests and third-party conformance testing; track OCPP 2.1 and ISO 15118-20 readiness.  

**Architecture and engineering partnership**

Partner with .NET Core architects on an event-driven microservices design that handles tens of thousands of concurrent WebSocket sessions, high-frequency MeterValues ingestion, and exactly-once transaction handling.  

Set and enforce non-functional requirements: connection stability, message latency, offline transaction recovery, horizontal scalability, observability and multi-region failover.  
Review technical designs for protocol correctness, backward compatibility and operational risk before implementation starts.  
Ensure the platform exposes clean, versioned APIs for customer portals, mobile apps, fleet management systems, payment processors and OCPI partners.  

**Risk, dependency and quality management**

Identify and mitigate hardware-to-cloud compatibility risks, firmware update bottlenecks, certificate expiry, and cross-team dependencies before they affect field uptime.  

Own the incident review loop for protocol-related outages: root cause, corrective action, and roadmap change if the failure is structural.  
Define release quality bars: automated OCPP conformance tests, load tests against charger simulators, and staged rollouts with rollback criteria.  
Track and report platform KPIs: charger uptime, session success rate, transaction reconciliation accuracy, mean time to onboard a new charger model, and firmware campaign completion rate.  

**Stakeholder, vendor and customer management**

Act as the primary technical interface for charger manufacturers, firmware vendors, utilities, CPOs, eMSPs and enterprise fleet customers.  

Negotiate technical scope, timelines and acceptance criteria with vendors; hold them to delivery and escalate with evidence when they slip.  
Lead customer-facing technical onboarding for large deployments: integration design, cutover plans, pilot acceptance and hypercare.  
Drive hardware certification and compliance workstreams (UL/ETL listing, Energy Star, NEVI/CFI program requirements, utility make-ready and demand-response integrations) in coordination with hardware and compliance teams.  

**Security and compliance**

Own the OCPP 2.0.1 security program: security

new_jobs.title: Operations Analyst, Acquisitions & Inventory
new_jobs.description:
About Winston TCG

We're Winston TCG, a trading card company in Arcadia. We started about three years ago and we sell Pokémon cards on TikTok Shop, Whatnot, eBay, Shopify, Walmart, and Best Buy, with livestreams running most of the day. We buy a lot of our cards in Japan, grade them, and sell them on stream. We're also opening our first retail store here in Arcadia.

We're a young, fast-growing company, and we're looking for someone who wants to help build out the buying side of the business with us.

The role

This is a data role first. You'd own the numbers behind our card buying and grading operation — what we pay, what grades, what sells, what we net — and turn that into clean reporting leadership can act on each week. From there you'd keep cash and inventory tight and use what the data shows to guide the buyers on what to pick up and what to leave alone.

It's hands-on. You'll split your time between the spreadsheets and the card room.

Here's what you'd be responsible for:

* **The numbers.** Every stream, buying trip, and grading submission tracked: cost, sale price, fees, net. You'd build and own the weekly report — gross, net, margin, ROI by stream and by source — plus the numbers that drive buying decisions, like cost per graded 10, grading hit rate by source, and which cards and sets are actually moving on which platform. Getting that built is the first thing you'd do.
* **Cash.** Our buyers travel with cash to Japan and to shows. You'd issue it, log it, and reconcile every trip within a couple of days of the team getting back.
* **Inventory and the grading pipeline.** Cards come in, get checked, go out to grading, and come back for stream. You'd know where everything is, what it cost, and what it's worth at every step, and flag cards that aren't likely to grade well before we pay to submit them.
* **Guiding the buyers.** You won't be the one on the floor in Osaka. You'd build the buy lists and the rules the buyers work from — price ceilings, how many copies of a card we need, what's selling and what isn't — and check trip lists against inventory before anyone spends money.
* **The room.** Inventory organized and labeled well enough that when a host asks for a card, someone can find it fast.
* **The team's day to day.** Coordinating schedules and output for the buyers and processors, helping train new people, and giving leadership an honest read on how things are going.
* **Shows and trips.** Supporting card-show runs and Japan trips from the office: buy lists, cash, logistics, and the numbers review afterward.

About you

I don't care much about where you worked before. I care about how you work. The people who do well here have good common sense, keep real numbers, and don't need to be told twice. Here's what I'm looking for:

* You live in spreadsheets. Hand you a messy export and you'll come back with the three numbers that matter, not a 20-tab workbook.
* You're tight with cash. Every dollar is accounted for, every trip is reconciled, and you don't need reminding.
* You handle curve balls. Shipment's late, show was a bust, someone bought off the list — you deal with it that day and then put a rule in place so it doesn't happen again.
* You have good sense. I'll give you the goal and the context. I won't always have a procedure written down, and I need you to make the right call anyway.
* You tell me straight. If something's not working, I want to hear it from you with the numbers, not find out later.
* You like cards or you're curious about them. You don't need to be a Pokémon expert — the team has that — but you'll need to learn how to check condition in your first couple of months.

Requirements

**Must have**

* Bachelor's degree, ideally in business, accounting, finance, economics, supply chain, or something similar
* 3+ years running day-to-day operations where you were directly accountable for inventory or cash: retail, warehouse, e-commerce, or a business you ran yourself
* Advanced Excel / Google Sheets: pivot tables, lookups, and tracking sheets you built from scratch. We'll ask you to take a short Excel test before the first interview.
* Hands-on experience handling and reconciling cash
* Experience coordinating a small team's daily work
* Valid passport and willingness to travel to Japan; valid driver's license for card shows
* Able to pass a background check (this role handles cash and inventory)
* Able to work on-site in Arcadia, CA five days a week
* Authorized to work in the United States

**Nice to have**

* Trading-card experience: buying, selling, or grading (Pokémon, TCG, sports cards)
* Whatnot, eBay, or TikTok Shop selling experience at volume
* Startup or early-stage company experience
* Japanese language ability
* Experience building SOPs and training documents

Compensation and schedule

* **Pay:** $65,000 to $85,000 a year depending on your experience
* **Bonus:** A quarterly bonus based on how the acquisitions team does on net margin. We'll spend the first 90 days together setting fair targets before it kicks in.
* **Schedule:** Full-time, in person at our Arcadia office, Monday through Friday. Some weekends for card shows, and probably one or two trips to Japan a year.
* **Where this goes:** The buying side of the business is growing, and this role grows with it.
* **Benefits:** Paid time off and employee pricing on product

Winston TCG is an equal opportunity employer.

Pay: $65,000.00 - $85,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Employee discount

Application Question(s):

* How many years have you managed day-to-day operations with direct accountability for inventory or cash
* Rate your Excel/Google Sheets skill: Basic / Intermediate / Advanced
* Have you personally handled and reconciled cash in a previous job?
* Have you coordinated or led the daily work of a team of 3 or more?

Education:

* Bachelor's (Required)

Work Location: In person

* Experience in software support, business systems, quality assurance, lending operations, or product development preferred.

new_jobs.title: Program Manager, Accounting Operations & Strategy
new_jobs.description:
**About Anthropic**
-------------------

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

**About the role**
------------------

Anthropic is seeking a Program Manager to join our Accounting organization and help it run as one global team. Accounting is scaling at an unprecedented pace across multiple hubs, and the goals, rhythms, programs, and people that make up the team need to stay connected as we grow. In this role, you will own that connective tissue: the annual goal-setting cycle, the leadership team’s operating cadence, org-wide events and internal communications, and the programs that make a distributed team feel like one.

You will partner with Accounting leadership, the People team, Finance Systems, and hub leads. This is a hands-on role with a lot of range: part chief of staff, part program manager, part culture builder.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

### **Goals and operating rhythm**

* Run the annual goal setting process and the reporting that tracks progress against those goals.
* Look at how the org actually operates (meetings, handoffs, planning cycles, decision making) and fix what isn't working.
* Maintain one org-wide planning calendar that shows close, audit, and team milestones alongside company-wide and team events, so leaders can see the pressure points and plan around them.
* Build and maintain a simple set of org health metrics (attrition, engagement scores, hiring pipeline, training completion, survey trends) and report on them regularly.

### **Leadership and org-wide events**

* Run our extended leadership team (XLT) program, including agendas, meetings, follow-ups, and action items.
* Own planning and agenda for the annual offsite and run the quarterly team all-hands.
* Write the internal updates: a regular team newsletter, plus talking points when leadership needs to explain a change to the whole org.

### **People and culture**

* Coordinate projects across the org that support employee experience programs.
* Partner with the People team to roll out training and development programs for Accounting.
* Review team survey results, identify the themes, and build action plans to address the feedback. Follow through and report back to the team.
* Run hub programs, including visit and rotation programs, local hub events, and meeting norms that work across time zones, so we feel like one global team.
* Run recognition and team rituals: wins, milestones, anniversaries, and peer recognition, especially across hubs.

### **Team operations**

* Support contractor management, including onboarding, tracking, and coordination with the right partners.
* Keep the team's knowledge base current: wiki, org charts, role descriptions, and key process docs.
* Keep the team calendar accurate so everyone knows what's coming.

**Preferred qualifications**
----------------------------

* 7+ years in program management, operations, chief of staff, or strategy roles. Experience inside a finance or accounting org is a plus, but not required.
* A track record of running recurring programs end to end and getting people to follow through without formal authority.
* Good judgment about what matters and what doesn't. You can handle a lot of moving pieces without dropping them.
* Clear, direct writing. You can brief a senior leader in a few sentences.
* Comfort with confidential information and sensitive people topics.
* Experience supporting distributed or global teams.
* You're organized, but you also know when a process is getting in the way and should be simplified.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

$230,000 - $300,000 USD

**Logistics**
-------------

**Minimum education:** Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

**Required field of study:** A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

**Minimum years of experience:** Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

**Location-based hybrid policy:** Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

**Visa sponsorship:** We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

**We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.** Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.  
  
**Your safety matters to us.** To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains.

**Who We Are:**

Hewlett Packard Enterprise is the global edge-to-cloud company advancing the way people live and work. We help companies connect, protect, analyze, and act on their data and applications wherever they live, from edge to cloud, so they can turn insights into outcomes at the speed required to thrive in today’s complex world. Our culture thrives on finding new and better ways to accelerate what’s next. We know varied backgrounds are valued and succeed here. We have the flexibility to manage our work and personal needs. We make bold moves, together, and are a force for good. If you are looking to stretch and grow your career our culture will embrace you. Open up opportunities with HPE.

**Job Description:**

**Role Description**

The **Complex Program Manager (CPM)** is a key leadership role within HPE’s Private Cloud and Flex Solutions business, responsible for delivering large-scale, multi-site private cloud solutions as a single integrated program. In this role, you will coordinate multiple HPE technologies, including compute, storage, networking, and software, alongside Deployment Services, Professional Services, Managed Services, Local PMOs, third-party partners, and customer teams to achieve successful business outcomes.

The CPM engages early in the sales lifecycle as part of the Center of Excellence pursuit team, helping ensure solutions are deliverable as sold. From initial order and factory build (Day 0), through deployment (Day 1), migration activities (Day 2), and transition into Managed Services operations (Day M), you will provide end-to-end program leadership. This highly visible role requires strong governance, executive-level communication, and the ability to drive alignment across diverse stakeholders while delivering some of HPE’s most innovative and complex solutions.

Success in this position requires a combination of program management expertise, technical acumen, relationship management, cross-functional leadership, and meticulous attention to detail.

**What Makes This Role Complex**

The CPM leads programs that integrate multiple HPE products into a single customer solution, while direct ownership of those products remains with separate business units. Networking, compute, storage, and software offerings each follow independent roadmaps and release cycles. Program delivery responsibilities are distributed across the CPMO, Local PMOs, Engineering, Managed Services, partners, and customer teams. The CPM is accountable for driving alignment, managing dependencies, resolving issues, escalating risks, and leading recovery efforts whenever program outcomes are at risk.

* Lead structured handoff and transition reviews at each major program phase (pursuit to order, factory to site, deployment to operations), ensuring documented entry and exit criteria are met.

**End-to-End Schedule Management**

* Own and maintain the integrated master schedule from order through delivery and execution, ensuring alignment with product release timelines, material availability, dependencies, and critical path activities.

**Operating Model**

**Escalation Management**

* Identify and communicate issues early, including business impact assessments and recovery plans.

**Risk and Change Management**

* Maintain a comprehensive RAID (Risks, Assumptions, Issues, and Dependencies) log as the program’s single source of truth, ensuring every item has a defined owner, mitigation strategy, and target completion date.
* Drive formal change control processes for scope, schedule, and cost impacts.

new_jobs.title: Principal, Program Manager Source to Pay - AI Workflow
new_jobs.description:
**Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for** ***all*****.**

Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

Micron is looking for a Program Manager, Source to Pay (S2P) Transformation – AI Workflows steer a multi-year change in the Source to Pay AI value stream. AI will be key in how tasks are composed and performed. The transformation agenda spans data, processes, platforms, and people to fundamentally reimagine the future of work.

The Lead of the S2P AI Workflow Tower owns the future-state design and end-to-end execution of the AI-first, agentic workflows that sit at the core of Micron's Source-to-Pay transformation. This is a builder-operator role: you will partner directly with the S2P transformation leadership to shape where the AI tower is going, then own the delivery of those workflows into production by orchestrating GPSC (Global Procurement Supply Chain) business teams, IT, and stakeholders across a matrixed program.

This role is central to driving the prioritized agentic flows from requirements and design through build, testing, deployment, and scale. The ideal candidate blends an AI-first mindset with strong business acumen and disciplined program management, and is equally comfortable in an architecture conversation, a business-requirements workshop, and an executive steering review.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Shape the future-state AI workflow strategy.** Partner with S2P leadership to define the vision, roadmap, and prioritization for the AI tower's agentic workflows — designing from the future, not from today, and challenging current-state assumptions.
* **Own end-to-end execution of AI workflows.** Drive prioritized agentic flows (e.g., Tactical Sourcing, Accounts Payable, and follow-on flows) from business requirements and design through build, UAT, deployment, and scale into production.
* **Translate business needs into AI-first solutions.** Convert procurement and AP process requirements into agent designs, user stories, and business rules, ensuring solutions are fit-for-purpose and not over-engineered.
* **Lead the tower's delivery cadence.** Run the tower's weekly connects and represent the tower in the S2P Operating Committee; manage the workplan, backlog, and sprints (Azure DevOps) with clear owners, dates, and milestones.
* **Partner across GPSC business, IT, and stakeholders.** Coordinate business SMEs, IT (Solutions, Enterprise Architecture, Data), AP/Finance, and the Deloitte delivery team to unblock work and keep workflows moving to plan.
* **Own the tower's RAID and key design decisions.** Maintain risks, actions, issues, decisions, and assumptions in the program system of record (Smartsheet); bring well-framed Key Design Decisions (KDDs) to governance with options and a recommendation, not just a problem.
* **Manage cross-tower dependencies.** Proactively surface and resolve dependencies and blockers spanning other towers (Buying Channels, Catalog, Data Management, Contract Compliance, Ariba, Supplier Invoicing) and adjacent programs (S4, Ironclad).
* **Embed AI governance, security, and compliance.** Ensure agentic workflows adhere to Micron's AI governance policy, AI model/system security standards, and SOX/policy controls — designing compliance into the workflow rather than bolting it on.
* **Drive adoption and operating-model change.** Partner on change management, role/responsibility redesign, and training so the human-machine hybrid workforce is operationalized and adopted, not just built.
